line: The Empire State's 1931 brochure credits its builders; the site film and Hine's photos answer: 2,500 a day.
line_cn: 帝国大厦的小册子写着建造者，工地实拍和老照片给出答案：每天 2,500 人。

motion.cuts: camera-led cuts: slide or push-through on motion

camera.expresses: one tempo for picture and score (120 BPM: beat 0.5 s, bar 2 s). Every cut, slam, wipe and count lands on a beat, half-beat or sixteenth. The page exports these times as window.EV; the mix reads the sa
0.5–2 s for footage; one idea per shot. A section may accelerate by halving: 0.5 → 0.25 → 0.125 s (never shorter than 3 frames). Holds are reserved for reading: a text block, a freeze, a comparison.
adjacent shots conflict in at least one of direction (left slam / right slam), value (paper / ink ground), or geometry (diagonal band / upright window). Never two paper documents in a row.

camera.move: Nothing static for more than a second
camera.expresses: inside a hold something moves (film in its window, a counter, a slow push, a frame-within-the-frame). Planned exceptions only: the comparison hold, one silence beat, the end card.

camera.move: Transitions inside the medium (pick per cut, don't fade)

camera.expresses: a 260 px red band at 72° (perpendicular to the axis) sweeps the frame in 0.25 s, the next scene revealed behind it; it lands on the downbeat;
a red marker circle drawn on a map or photo becomes an aperture and opens onto footage;
the next element arrives from outside along the axis in 0.08–0.2 s, ease-out, hard stop, frame shake (amplitude 3–18 px, exp(−14·Δt));
one frame of 50–80 % paper over a window at a cut or freeze;

camera.move: hard cut on the beat between grounds of opposite value;

camera.expresses: inside a freeze, a cut to a 1.2× crop of the same frame, the annotation scaling with it.
one where the orchestra stops and only an original recording remains, and one true half-bar of nothing (ink frame, one red dot) before the heaviest hit.

transitions: Every cut, slam, wipe and count lands on a beat, half-beat or sixteenth.
Cut rule: adjacent shots conflict in at least one of direction (left slam / right slam), value (paper / ink ground), or geometry (diagonal band / upright window).
Transitions inside the medium (pick per cut, don't fade): - red wipe: a 260 px red band at 72° (perpendicular to the axis) sweeps the frame in 0.25 s, the next scene revealed behind it;
flash cut: one frame of 50–80 % paper over a window at a cut or freeze;
labels: Bilingual pairs: Chinese block, then one English line in Oswald directly under it (or on the neighbouring band). Each language one line, measured.
Placement: along the −18° axis on a band, or as an ink / red block; never centred on the frame, never a header. Numbers can be bigger than the words that explain them.

Tags: every archive window carries its footage tag (FILM · <TITLE> · <PLACE> <YEAR>, PHOTO · <AUTHOR> <YEAR>), every fact a source tag (来源 · <PUBLISHER> <YEAR>). If the footage is not of the subject itself, the tag says what it really is.

Subtitles stay bottom-left in a 960–1056 px strip; key type keeps above y 930 while narration runs. Subtitles hold ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s). On-screen text follows readcheck.mjs (CJK ÷ 4.5 + other ÷ 15 + 1.5 s, fully in frame); a comparison holds every item ≥ 2.5 s before its verdict.

native_moves.name: The document is marked, not quoted
native_moves.does: the actual sentence on the scan gets a red bar; the number then becomes a red block.

native_moves.name: The document becomes the chart
native_moves.does: drawings printed on a page are lifted off, turned and stood on a ground line to scale.

native_moves.name: A + B → idea
native_moves.does: two kinds of image alternate faster and faster (the machine / the hands; a heading / the people it leaves out) until a card or a number states what the collision meant.

native_moves.name: Count the many
native_moves.does: a counter driven by the cuts, a grid that fills cell by cell, a tower floor by floor.

native_moves.name: People build the structure
native_moves.does: cut-out figures stacked into the thing they made (photomontage).

score.note: machine ostinato in spiccato cellos and bassoon, staccato tuba, snare, xylophone
